analysis: The changed file is fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json, a golden-vector fixture. The visible patch only replaces prompt_contract_id values and the derived block chain_hash and last_complete_block_hash values. These changes cover the EigenLabs/Qwen3.8-27B-4bit-mtp, gemma-4-26b, gemma-4-26b-8bit, gemma-4-26b-qat-4bit and gpt-oss-20b model entries. In the supplied hunks, token_ids, prompt_token_count, block token_count and cache_routing_eligible are unchanged. Nothing in this fixture changes trust boundaries, authentication, encryption, attestation, billing or authorization. The consistent per-model remapping looks like a deliberate contract-version regeneration. The prompt contract ID and chain hashes feed the prefix-cache keying and routing described in T-041 (cross-tenant prefix-cache sharing). Changing these values only invalidates existing cache artifacts, which is a fail-safe direction. Only the fixture is in the supplied evidence, so I could not verify these questions. First, whether the producer code (prompt-contract hashing in the Swift provider or the backend) was changed to match, with no stale vectors left in either implementation. Second, whether the contract-ID derivation still binds all security-relevant inputs, such as the tenant or cache salt, so that T-041 cross-tenant isolation is unaffected. The patch excerpt and range map are incomplete, since the diff is truncated mid-hunk at the gpt-oss-20b entry. I found no concrete security regression in the visible lines. The producer and consumer code paths and the truncated remainder should be checked in a later pass.
